instructions: Use keyWords as the answers/keys across TC blanks and SE pairs (29 slots, order free); key each of the sePairs (two key words that are bank synonyms) as one SE item; any other SE item pairs a key word with a listed bank synonym. Draw at least 75% of the distractor words from distractorWords.untested, the rest from distractorWords.weak. Weave 5-6 passageWords into each RC passage (not the arguments). check enforces both. Do not write word tags: `npm run tag` fills them from the choice and passage text (regular inflections match; tag an irregular form such as `forsworn` by hand). Each key word's `sense` is the GRE-tested sense: write the sentence so THAT sense is the one that fits (for secondary=true words, the everyday sense must be the trap). Give each RC question one primary skill tag {kind:'concept', role:'primary'} from skillSlots (argument skills on the arg items, rc-select-verify suits rc_multi), optionally a secondary one; the reading skills can repeat. Write each skill slot's question as its `variant`. A key word that was used before comes back in a new sentence logic, with a new SE partner where possible, and with no distractor from its earlier items (the validator rejects a shared distractor or a repeated SE pair). A key word with a `revisit` is a deliberate sibling of that earlier item, made with the change named: set `revisits` to its ref on the question. typeFocus ranks question types by practice need (miss rate plus slowness against pace): put the weakest review words / skills / concepts on the slots of the top two types (need >= 0.4), so the practice lands where it is needed.
